title: From access to judgement
text: India has over a billion internet users, but only 18% of adults can file a cybercrime complaint online. As generative AI makes fakes cheap, 'the question is no longer how to access information, but how to judge what is reliable'. Children meet AI-shaped feeds before they can question them.
use: For 'A well-educated mind will always have more questions than answers' (2026) and 'Biased media is a real threat to Indian democracy' (2019).

title: The girl whose questions outran her teachers
text: Diksha Nagarkoti grew up in Pithoragarh, on the Indo-Nepal border, watching the mountains change with the seasons and wondering how ecosystems worked. Her teachers could not answer all her questions. She found her answers through VigyanShaala's STEM mentors; over 20,000 young women, most of them first-generation learners, have joined its She for STEM programme.
use: Open or illustrate: 'A well-educated mind will always have more questions than answers' (2026), 'The Empires of the future will be the empires of the mind' (2024).

title: Jogen Chowdhury: refugee to master painter
text: Born into a landed family in Faridpur in pre-Partition East Bengal, he suffered a great reversal of fortune and became a post-Partition refugee in Calcutta. Drawing on memories of the kantha embroidery and alpona floor art of Bengal's village women, he built a personal modern idiom. The tribute calls him a 'hard optimist' and a 'dreamer of institutions'.
use: For 'A thorn is a changed bud', 'Best lessons are learnt through bitter experiences' and 'magical in the mundane' (art from folk floor drawings).

title: Lycurgus Cup and Roman concrete: the science in 'magic'
text: A 1,600-year-old Roman cup glows red in normal light and green when lit from behind. Scientists have only now reverse-engineered it. Roman concrete is still not fully recreated, and Indus Valley drainage still has lessons for cities. The editorial argues that the past's real magic is useful achievement, not myths of flying chariots.
use: For 'magical in the mundane', 'The doubter is a true man of science' (versus pseudo-history) and 'Culture is what we are, civilisation is what we have'.

title: The farmer who copied a friend's strawberries
text: In Manauli, Sonipat, Arun Chauhan switched from paddy to sweet corn after visiting a friend's strawberry farm. His village moved 70% of its land to sweet corn and vegetables, formed an FPO and now sells directly to e-commerce firms.
use: For 'The cost of being wrong is less than the cost of doing nothing', 'Ideas with large consequences are simple' and 'A ship in harbour is safe'.
